# Task 13 — Print-friendly workflow report

**Status:** active  
**Scope:** Browser printing and Save as PDF for the self-contained, per-sample workflow report generated by `scripts/p6_report.py`.  
**Source:** [qcif/taxodactyl#366](https://github.com/qcif/taxodactyl/issues/366). No feature directory is configured. This brief uses `spec/python/p6-report.md`, the report templates and the core Selenium suite.  
Implementation authorization: pending explicit user instruction

## Overview

A reader can click through five tabs and open supporting evidence on screen. Printing currently hides inactive tabs and closed dialogs. Make the printed document readable from beginning to end, with the evidence beside the result it explains and reference tables at the back. An analyst should be able to print the report before or after recording a conclusion. The user will judge the finished layout from sample PDFs.

## Preconditions

Use the existing report context and inline assets described in P6-001 and preserve the saved-copy behavior in P6-004. For validation, use retained per-query inputs with P4 source diversity and P5 database coverage results and at least one report with absent or unassessed results. Record the workflow revision, sample IDs, reference-data versions from the run and browser version for each review artifact.

## Objective

From any tab, the browser's Print command produces the same section order and complete evidence for that sample. Print the analyst's current answers, including unanswered prompts. Returning to the screen preserves the analyst's place and selections.

## Implementation

Paths below the report package are relative to `scripts/src/report/`.

1. **Linearize the report.** In `templates/index.html`, `templates/components/content-tabs.html` and `static/css/main.css`, scope print rules to the workflow report. Show Overview, Results summary, Candidate species, Taxa of interest and Conclusions in their screen order with visible headings. Suppress tab navigation, modal backdrops, buttons and click instructions. Let tables flow across pages, repeat table headers, wrap long identifiers and size images to the printable width. Check these rules with only the first tab visited.
2. **Place reference tables after Conclusions.** Reuse the hit rows in `templates/components/results/1a-blast-hits-modal.html` and definitions in `templates/components/flags-modal.html`. Give each appendix a heading and identify it where the reader would normally open the modal. Include every BLAST row despite the modal's height limit or a species filter. Keep hit-specific selection panes out of the printed summary table. Respect the BLAST/BOLD condition in `templates/components/results/1-candidate-species.html`. The issue names the BLAST hit appendix; the common sections also apply to BOLD reports.
3. **Put P4/P5 details next to their results.** Reuse `templates/components/results/3-source-diversity-modal.html` and `templates/macros/db-coverage-target-modal.html`. Group each applicable detail block under its taxon and role in `templates/components/results/1-candidate-species.html`, `templates/components/results/2-taxa-of-interest.html` and `templates/components/conclusions/pmi-table.html`. Account for TOI dialogs currently inserted by `templates/components/results/toi-modals.html` at the page end. Preserve warnings, missing-data messages, tables and maps. Render each applicable block once per role, with unique DOM IDs and valid table markup. Check the shared macro's existing caller in `templates/coverage/index.html` when changing its interface.
4. **Print the analyst's answers.** Use `templates/macros/yes_no_buttons.html` and `templates/components/conclusion-checklist.html` to show labelled static Yes/No boxes reflecting the current radio state. Leave both empty when unanswered. Preserve the visible follow-up branch. In `templates/components/conclusions.html` and `templates/macros/subjective.html`, make entered notes readable in full even when the Conclusions tab has never been opened. Verify the same behavior in a copy saved by `static/js/save-report.js`.
5. The appendix, inline evidence and answer rendering can proceed independently after the print structure is established. Integrate all three before PDF review.

## Documentation and configuration

Record the browser-print contract alongside the page structure in `spec/python/p6-report.md`. The normal entry point is the browser's existing print command on a generated HTML report.

## Testing decision

On 2026-11-25 the user assigned the agent to write targeted print assertions and run the automated checks for issue #366. The user reviews sample PDFs and output drift and owns all changes to expected results, including Selenium fixtures, snapshots and flag baselines. Implementation and manual acceptance are both pending.

## Validation

- Generate fresh HTML with the candidate templates. Use the **P6 Workflow report** launch configuration in `.vscode/launch.json` with the retained query directory and its matching FASTA, metadata and run parameters. The generated file is `<query_dir>/report_[BOLD_]<sample_id>_<timestamp>.html`. Use reports from the same inputs and data versions when comparing revisions.
- Extend `test/selenium/test_reports.py` with targeted print-media checks using representative existing samples. Verify section order, appendix membership and row count against independently inspected inputs, and taxon/role labels for P4/P5. Exercise Yes, No and unanswered states, multi-line notes, and return to screen media. Preserve the screen-mode assertions and reset browser state between cases.
- From the repository root activate the environment with `source scripts/venv/bin/activate`. With the Selenium dependencies installed, run `cd test/selenium` then `pytest test_reports.py -v --dir /absolute/path/to/generated/core/reports` against the complete core report set. Record the revision, commands, passes and failures. Investigate any discrepancy before proposing an expectation change.
- Save representative PDFs beside their source HTML in a scratch review directory. Include a multi-page BLAST appendix, candidate and TOI coverage, an absent/unassessed result, and examples of answered and unanswered conclusions. Include a reopened saved copy. Give the user the paths and the sample/page to inspect for each case. Check first and last hit rows, clipped columns or maps, overlapping sections, blank pages and checkbox legibility. Leave visual acceptance pending until the user records the result.

## Test impact and manual review

`test/selenium/test_reports.py` collects screen content through `test/selenium/lib/collect.py`. New print markup can duplicate matches for its screen selectors. Existing values in `test/selenium/expected/*.yaml` and reference HTML in `test/selenium/expected/reports/` are user-owned. Compare `test/selenium/test-report.json` and `test/selenium/review.html` with the generated HTML when a screen assertion fails.

The self-hosted job in `.github/workflows/nf-test.yml` runs `nf-test test test/core/taxodactyl.workflow.nf.test` and the Selenium command above. The workflow test counts HTML outputs and snapshots upstream channels. A layout change has no expected scientific effect on `test/core/taxodactyl.workflow.nf.test.snap` or `test/core/flags/`. Refer any observed differences to the user with run provenance. Keep fixture updates and PDF acceptance separate from passing automated checks.

## Completion criteria

The generated offline HTML prints all applicable sections, appendices, evidence and analyst answers in the specified order. Existing screen navigation, modal interactions and saved-copy behavior pass regression checks. Record automated results, unresolved failures and the user's PDF review separately. Close the task after the user accepts the representative PDFs and resolves any baseline differences.
